title: Thomas Lott: Barry Switzer's Wishbone Quarterback, 1976-78
question: Who was Thomas Lott, the Oklahoma wishbone quarterback of the late 1970s?
answer: Thomas Lott, a San Antonio native, started at quarterback for Oklahoma from 1976 to 1978, earned All-Big Eight honors in 1977 and 1978, and was called the greatest wishbone quarterback in Sooner history by coach Barry Switzer.
summary: Thomas Lott ran Barry Switzer's wishbone at Oklahoma from 1976 to 1978, earning All-Big Eight honors twice and three conference titles. Here is his story.
body: For three seasons in the late 1970s, the Sooner wishbone belonged to a quarterback from San Antonio. Thomas Lott (OU 1976-78) came out of John Jay High School, where he ran the wishbone, topped 1,000 rushing yards as both a junior and a senior, and was a Parade All-American after the 1974 season, according to the Texas High School Football Hall of Fame profile.

Lott signed with Oklahoma and took over the offense in 1976, running it for three seasons under Barry Switzer. The San Antonio Sports Hall of Fame notes that the Sooners won three Big Eight titles during his time on campus. The 1977 team finished 10-1 and was ranked sixth nationally, with Lott leading the club in rushing.

The league's coaches and media took notice too. Lott was named All-Big Eight in 1977 and again in 1978, a season in which the Sooners also featured Sims in the backfield. Switzer later called him the greatest wishbone quarterback in Oklahoma history, a remarkable compliment in a program that ran that offense for years.

Lott was drafted by the St. Louis Cardinals in the sixth round of the 1979 NFL Draft. He later returned kickoffs for the New Jersey Generals of the USFL in 1983. Note that published sources differ on some of his season rushing totals and starting record, so this post sticks to the honors and dates they agree on.
